_frozen_by: claude (Bench desk), built and API-verified 2026-09-05 at Adam's direction
_status: FROZEN. Never edit this file. If the universe must change, create universe-core-v2.json ALONGSIDE it and record which version each daily row was collected under.
_purpose: The DENOMINATOR for a pre-pump base rate. Every one of these names is recorded every trading day whether or not it does anything. The boring rows are the dataset; without them a hit rate cannot be computed.
_provenance: Every symbol was verified live through get_equity_fundamentals during the freeze session. Nothing here is an unverified guess. All *_at_freeze values are the provider values AT FREEZE TIME and are deliberately never updated - they are the point-in-time record against which later drift is measured.

_selection_method.approach: Stratified by market-cap band, spread across FactSet-style sectors, then independently audited by a separate agent that spot-checked 20 rows against the live feed.

bands.LOWPRICE: $0.20 - $5.00 by PRICE, any market cap, >= $1M/day dollar volume. The pump-dense population a price floor would have deleted.

_selection_method.weighting: Deliberately overweight small and micro relative to market-cap weight, because that is where the phenomenon being hunted concentrates, while retaining a real mega/large negative mass so the base rate has a boring majority.

_floors.price: >= $0.20 at freeze. The original $1.00 floor was REMOVED - see _amendment_note. Dollar volume, not price, is the liquidity gate.
_floors.dollar_volume_note: REPLACED the original 100,000-share floor after the audit showed a share-count floor is price-blind: it admitted names trading $256k/day. At that size one retail order moves the print and fabricates the exact signature this dataset exists to measure.
_floors.instrument: US-listed common stock only. No ETFs, funds, trusts, or crypto tickers. Verified: every row has a non-null float and is_etf_or_fund false.

_known_limitations: SURVIVORSHIP: every name was chosen on 2026-09-05 and has therefore already survived to that date. This list cannot measure anything about companies that died before it was frozen. A base rate computed from it is conditional on survival to the freeze date and must be reported that way.

DELISTING: when a name is acquired, delisted or halted, the collector MUST keep emitting a row with nulls and a status, not silently drop it. A shrinking denominator inflates every rate computed from it.

SMALL-CAP BATCH ARTIFACT: SMALL_A and SMALL_B were assembled as sector-defined halves. SMALL_A is ~37% Health Technology by construction. THEY MUST ALWAYS BE USED TOGETHER as one SMALL band. A base rate drawn from SMALL_A alone is a biotech base rate wearing a small-cap label.

FLOAT/CAP BASIS MISMATCH: market_cap is computed on all share classes while float is a single-class free-float figure. float_to_shares_ratio is recorded per row so analysis can condition on it; float/cap ratios are NOT comparable across rows without it.

PROVIDER SECTOR LABELS ARE KEPT VERBATIM AND NOT CORRECTED. 18 rows carry labels the audit disputes (AAPL as Telecommunications Equipment, NATR as Health Technology, CLB as Energy Minerals, eight E&Ps as Integrated Oil, and others). They are FLAGGED via sector_label_disputed rather than rewritten, because overwriting a provider value with our own judgement would put a fiction in a point-in-time dataset. Filter on the flag before computing any sector-conditioned base rate.
BRCC band is uncertain (Up-C structure, Class-A-only share count). Flagged band_uncertain; exclude from band-conditioned analysis.

FROZEN METADATA GOES STALE BY DESIGN. Market cap, float and volume at freeze are a snapshot. Band membership is reproducible only against the freeze date, which is why every value carries the _at_freeze suffix.

LOWPRICE band is by construction ~60pct Health Technology (biotech dominates the sub-$5 liquid population). Like SMALL_A/SMALL_B, do not compute a base rate from this band alone and call it a market rate.

_amendment_note: AMENDED ONCE, BEFORE ANY DATA WAS COLLECTED, and never again. The original build used a price >= $1.00 floor. That floor deletes the phenomenon: GPRO traded $4.28M-$5.38M/day at ~$0.60 in the three sessions before a +181.7pct move on 24.5x volume, and it is the clearest positive in the book. A LOWPRICE band ($0.20-$5.00 by price, >= $1,000,000/day dollar volume, common stock only) was verified and merged. Because zero rows had been collected, amending was strictly better than freezing a denominator known to exclude the target population. From this point the file is sealed: any further change is universe-core-v2.json alongside, never an edit.
